The '''1971–72 DDR-Oberliga''' was the 23rd season of the [[DDR-Oberliga]], the first tier of [[East German football league system|league football]] in [[East Germany]].

The league was contested by fourteen teams. [[1. FC Magdeburg]] won the championship, the club's first of three East German championships.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablesd/ddrchamp.html |title= East Germany - List of Champions |website= [[RSSSF]] |access-date= 26 January 2016}}</ref><ref name="Meister" >{{cite web |url=https://www.dfb.de/historie/ddr-fussball/meister/ |title= DDR-Meister |website=dfb.de |publisher=[[German Football Association]] |access-date= 26 January 2016|language=de|trans-title= East German champions}}</ref>

[[Hans-Jürgen Kreische]] of Dynamo Dresden was the league's top scorer with 14 goals, the second of a record four top scorer finishes for Kreische,<ref name="Goal" >{{cite web |url=http://www.weltfussball.de/torschuetzenkoenige/gdr-oberliga/ |title= DDDR » Oberliga » Torschützenkönige  |website= Weltfussball.de |access-date= 25 January 2016|language=de|trans-title=DDR-Oberliga top scorers }}</ref> while [[Jürgen Croy]] of [[FSV Zwickau|BSG Sachsenring Zwickau]] won the seasons [[Footballer of the Year in Germany|East German Footballer of the year]] award.<ref>''fuwo'', page: 92</ref>

On the strength of the 1971–72 title Magdeburg qualified for the [[1972–73 European Cup]] where the club was knocked out by [[Juventus FC|Juventus]] in the second round. Fourth-placed club [[FC Carl Zeiss Jena]] qualified for the [[1972–73 European Cup Winners' Cup]] as the seasons [[FDGB-Pokal]] winners and was knocked out by [[Leeds United]] in the second round. Second-placed [[BFC Dynamo]] qualified for the [[1972–73 UEFA Cup]] where it was knocked out in the third round by [[Liverpool F.C.]] while third-placed [[Dynamo Dresden]] lost to the same club in the quarter-finals.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.rsssf.org/ec/ec197273.html |title= European Competitions 1972-73 |website= [[RSSSF]] |access-date= 26 January 2016}}</ref>

Before the start of the season [[army]] club [[1. FC Frankfurt|FC Vorwärts Berlin]], based in [[East Berlin]], was moved to [[Frankfurt (Oder)|Frankfurt/Oder]] to become FC Vorwärts Frankfurt/Oder after a decision by the Ministry of Defence.<ref>{{cite news |last=Müller |first=Ronny |date=18 December 2015 |title=Club der Bessergestellten |url=https://www.sportbuzzer.de/artikel/club-der-bessergestellten/ |language=German |newspaper=[[Sportbuzzer]] |location=Hannover |publisher=Sportbuzzer GmbH|access-date=19 December 2021 }}</ref> The exact reasons for the relocation has not been fully clarified.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.rbb24.de/studiofrankfurt/sport/2021/08/fussball-frankfurt-ddr-oberliga-sport-pokal.html |title=Frankfurter DDR-Kicker feiern ihren Verein und alte Erfolge |last=Schwaß |first=Robert |date=14 August 2021 |website=www.rbb24.de |location=Berlin |publisher=[[Rundfunk Berlin-Brandenburg]] |language=German |access-date=19 December 2021 |archive-date=19 December 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211219125604/https://www.rbb24.de/studiofrankfurt/sport/2021/08/fussball-frankfurt-ddr-oberliga-sport-pokal.html |url-status=dead }}</ref> Vorwärts had been quite a popular club with East Berlin football supporters, but was seen as an obstacle to the ambitions of [[BFC Dynamo]]. BFC Dynamo was supported by the [[Stasi|Ministry for State Security]] and its head Erich Mielke.<ref>''fuwo'', page: 34 & 35</ref> The relocation was allegedly driven by Erich Mielke, who wanted to create better sporting conditions for BFC Dynamo in East Berlin, and his fellow Politburo member and [[Socialist Unity Party of Germany |SED]] First Secretary in [[Bezirk Frankfurt]] [[Erich Mückenberger]], who anticipated a boost for the Frankfurt/Oder region.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Mike |last2=Grix |first1=Dennis |first2=Jonathan |date=2012 |title=Sport under Communism – Behind the East German 'Miracle' |location=[[Hampshire]] |edition= 1st |publisher=Palgrave Macmillan (Macmillan Publishers Limited) |pages=138–139 |isbn=978-0-230-22784-2 }}</ref>
